raw_response:
I have been farming this land for over fifty years. My father farmed it before me, and his father before him. I know this land. I know what grows here, what the soil needs, and what the weather will bring.

In Quzhou, we all grow winter wheat and summer maize. Everyone on my road does it. The grain station buys it. My sons help me at harvest if I need it, but most of the work can be done by machine now — the tractor man comes through the village. If I tried something different, like vegetables or cotton, I would not know what to do with it, and the price is uncertain. Wheat and maize — I know the price, I know the buyer.

I have about 10 mu of flat land. Half I think of as the wheat plots, half the maize plots, but really it is the same land — wheat in winter, maize in summer, same fields. After the wheat comes off in June, I get the maize in quickly.

For seeds, I buy from the village supply shop. The improved wheat seed — they told me it yields better and resists rust. I believe them because I have seen it. For maize I always use hybrid seed. You cannot save hybrid seed, I know this, so I buy new every year. That is just how maize is now.

For fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer at sowing and then urea when the plants are growing. My neighbor uses the same amounts I do. We have always done it this way and the crops grow fine. Water — I pump from my well. Wheat needs water in winter and before the grain fills. Maize usually gets enough rain in summer, but if August is dry I pump once.

I am 68. My back is not good. I use rotary tillage before wheat — the tractor man does it. For maize I just seed directly into the wheat stubble without ploughing. Less work, and it seems fine.
